episode_title: E106: UAD 3.6 Data Ownership, Software Shakeup, Order Breakdown, Appraiser Concerns

real_qa.q: How many verified software providers are now available for UAD 3.6 appraisal reports as of the Appraisal Summit announcement?
real_qa.r: There are now 11 verified software providers to provide 3.6 appraisal reports, with an additional at least 17 more currently in the works going through the verification process at various stages. This represents two to three times more verified providers than historically existed in the legacy environment.

real_qa.q: What is the main concern appraisers have expressed about UAD 3.6 data ownership and usage?
real_qa.r: Appraisers are concerned that anybody who gets an appraisal can store, use, and distribute it in various ways. Data ownership and control over how completed appraisals are handled represents a significant pain point for the profession under the new standard.

real_qa.q: How many UAD 3.6 orders have been received since the November 2nd go-live date?
real_qa.r: Over 800 UAD 3.6 orders have been received, with the volume climbing week over week as reported across recent Market Moves episodes.

real_qa.q: What are the primary pain points appraisers face with UAD 3.6 order delivery beyond writing the report?
real_qa.r: The main pain points are not about how to write the report itself, but rather how to deliver it and actually get it to the client through all of the validation issues that arise in the process.

real_qa.q: When did UAD 3.6 go live for the mortgage appraisal industry?
real_qa.r: UAD 3.6 went live on November 2nd and represents the appraisal transition that has taken the country by storm over the last couple of years.

real_quote: I don't think a lot of these folks are still going to be around next year. There's just not enough appraisers to subscribe and support these softwares.
